feed.title: Field Notes — Steven Wensley
feed.subtitle: Short, sharp notes from 18 years of regulated delivery — and from inside a running AI factory.

entry.title: Leading extremely clever children with enormous power
entry.summary: They don't lack ethics. They have too much of the wrong kind — and it hides in the work they quietly don't do.

entry.title: When AI fabricates your control evidence
entry.summary: In a GxP, NIS2 or DORA environment, a hallucination isn't a wrong answer — it's an audit finding with a delay on it.

entry.title: Why your AI pilot is lying to you
entry.summary: Not maliciously. Structurally. An agent sounds equally confident when it has read the source and when it has invented one.

entry.title: "Done" is the most dangerous word in AI
entry.summary: A green test is not done. A merge is not done. A convincing explanation is nothing at all.

entry.title: One agent, seven hats — why your AI needs an org chart
entry.summary: The biggest AI failure in my factory wasn't a hallucination. It was an org-design error — mine.

entry.title: Why your SteerCo is lying to you
entry.summary: Amber is a negotiated colour — the colour of collective self-preservation.

entry.title: The first 7 days of a red programme
entry.summary: What I actually do in the first week of a takeover — and what I deliberately don't.

entry.title: NIS2: nobody's neck is on the line
entry.summary: The Danish transposition left out personal liability — and ownership evaporated with it.
